description:
**Surfaced 2026-05-17 by user-tier POLYBIUS during end-of-session hygiene audit.**

## The gap

The-stoa CLAUDE.md states: 'Forward work happens on a feature branch, not on main.' But user-tier POLYBIUS (this seat) has been committing housekeeping directly to local main throughout today's session — directive+activation-paste tracking commits, .gitignore narrowing, registry adds, retro doc, substrate-template frontmatter backfill, self-apply cleanups, etc. (~10+ commits direct to main today).

The CLAUDE.md rule reads as universal; the actual practice has an implicit exception for housekeeping. The substrate has no canon distinguishing what user-tier may commit to main vs what needs an arc.

## Why this matters

1. **Discipline coherence.** A universal rule with implicit exceptions is brittle. Future POLYBIUSes reading CLAUDE.md may either over-apply (refuse to do any direct-to-main commits, even hygiene) or under-apply (interpret 'forward work' narrowly + commit too much to main).

2. **Bundled-squash interaction.** Direct-to-main housekeeping commits create local-ahead state which interacts with the Arc 30 pre-branch hygiene discipline (push immediately to keep local = origin). Today's pattern relied on push-immediately to make this safe; without explicit canon, future POLYBIUSes may not.

3. **PR-history readability.** Housekeeping commits to main are not visible as arcs in git history (no PR squash; just standalone commits between arc-PRs). This is sometimes desirable (small fixes don't deserve full arc machinery) and sometimes confusing (no clear scope statement).

## Fix-shape options (DAEDALUS picks at design time)

### Option A — explicit user-tier housekeeping discipline

Encode in MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md (or operating-disciplines.md cross-ref) what user-tier may commit directly to main:
- Directive + activation paste tracking commits (Arc-N dispatch artifacts)
- Substrate-tool self-apply / drift-resolve commits
- Cleanup of orphan artifacts (worktree removals, etc.)
- bw ticket comments via bw commands (operates on orphan beadwork branch; not main)
- Retro docs at docs/sessions/

What requires an arc:
- Substrate canon edits (operating-disciplines.md, MAJOR_*.md, CAPTAIN_*.md, templates/, skills/)
- Tooling source changes (install.sh, check.sh, apply.sh)
- Anything that PLINY's gauntlet would normally cover

### Option B — strict: user-tier never commits to main; everything goes through an arc

Cleanest interpretation of current CLAUDE.md. But: would require dispatching a full PLINY arc for every small housekeeping change (like the substrate-template frontmatter backfill today, which was a 6-file edit that took ~5 min as a direct commit and would take ~30 min as a full arc).

Probably too restrictive; doesn't match how the substrate has empirically operated.

### Option C — update CLAUDE.md to acknowledge the exception explicitly

Edit CLAUDE.md's 'forward work on a feature branch' rule to read 'substantive forward work on a feature branch; user-tier housekeeping per MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §<section>.' Plus the §section in MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md per Option A.

Recommended composite: Option A + Option C (encode the discipline in canon, update CLAUDE.md to acknowledge).

## Acceptance

- Canon section exists naming what user-tier may direct-commit to main vs what needs arc-dispatch
- CLAUDE.md updated (if Option C) to cross-ref the canon
- Future POLYBIUSes reading the substrate cold can correctly identify whether a planned change requires an arc

## Out of scope

- Editing today's direct-to-main commits (history is history; can't unwind without rewriting; not worth)
- Other workspaces' similar gaps (this is the-stoa-specific; consumer workspaces have their own CLAUDE.md conventions)

## Cross-refs

- the-stoa CLAUDE.md ('Forward work happens on a feature branch, not on main' rule)
- Arc 30 stoa--3cs (PLINY pre-branch hygiene; interacts with user-tier direct-commits via local-ahead state)
- Today's session commit history (the empirical anchor — ~10+ direct-to-main commits over the day)

## Why P3

Real substrate discipline gap; recurring pattern (every session has direct-to-main commits); future POLYBIUSes need the canon. But not blocking — the implicit pattern works today; just want it explicit.
title: User-tier POLYBIUS commits to local main directly — substrate convention gap vs CLAUDE.md feature-branch rule
